A setting that can allow title posts or a verse to enable downvotes to be accompanied with a comment for feedback

It wouldn't discourage voting, if anything it encourages to vote for what you do like. And if it is downvoted for spam, then the comments can be seen as it being spam and action can be taken. it would address & present why submitted content is rejected. Either way you look at it, is has more positive benefits then negative.

It wouldn't be a system wide feature, but it can be enabled for posts or by the subverse. You may desire less interaction but comments are not pointless when they offer constructive criticism.

if anything it encourages to vote for what you do like

You're not explaining yourself. How exactly does restricting downvotes encourage people to upvote what they do like? There is no connection whatsoever.

And if it is downvoted for spam, then the comments can be seen as it being spam and action can be taken.

What about the other type I mentioned: 'stupid'? Those types of posts won't necessarily be breaking the rules, so they cannot be removed, but they'd be spammed with comments saying the exact same thing, flushing out any other comments talking about anything other than why it was downvoted. What I consider stupid may be cool to someone else. What about those who liked the post and want to read the comments and, perhaps, get involved in the discussion? It would be frustrating sorting through all of that junk.

it would address & present why submitted content is rejected

Couldn't it be done a better way? Like, perhaps, a separate thread discussing upvotes and downvotes?

Either way you look at it, is has more positive benefits then negative.

Positives:

  • A way to see why people don't like a post.

Negatives:

  • Less downvotes. It is a fact that adding a second step to any process will decrease the number of participants following through. Less contribution is bad.
  • More spam. More often than not, the number of downvotes will certainly exceed the reasons for the downvotes. This means that there will be comments saying the same thing, which is spam.

Contrarily, it has more cons than pros.

it can be enabled for posts or by the subverse

I think this would be a beneficial option for posts because it's giving the original posters the option of adopting the system. However, giving entire subverses the option to enable the feature for all posts may discourage posters that don't want to use the system, which could affect the health of that subverse. It could also affect the well being of the entire subverse because some posts will be completely run over with comments expressing downvoting reasons.

Controversial posts may be filled with spam, causing the discussion there to cease. Ultimately, we would see subverses with circlejerk hiveminds because those posts would be the only ones worth visiting and commenting.

  • Posts filled with spam

I feel like this was a powerful video because it shows that we can help change people's minds away from extremism. There is a lot to learn from such amazing story. These are the few important takeaways I got from this video:

  • Even though sometimes it is too late to help someone, like Zak's father, there is still hope in trying to help his children. We should keep this mind, and not punish the children, with intolerance and hatred, for the erroneous ways of the parent.

  • Experience is the strongest opponent of intolerance. You could have argued for days with Zak, while he was still under the care of his father, and he would have had great trouble giving up what he had learned from the years of teaching from his father. The greatest force against bigotry and hate, is to experience the love and get to know these people that you were taught to hate. People are less defensive against this, and they see for themselves why they were wrong, rather than being told why they are wrong.

  • As Zak so eloquently stated, we all have the freedom to make our choices. Just because everyone around (like Zak's uncles, dad, etc) is full of hatred, doesn't mean that we need to follow their footsteps. It will be difficult to go against the tide, but then again, as Zak says, it takes a whole lot of effort to hate and be intolerant.

  • Empathy is a powerful force. Our ability to empathize is an important factor that is necessary to create peace.
